rows.title: NFL wind: four Sunday totals to verify
rows.observation: The November 1 source selections are NE–MIA under 43.5 (-113), LAC–LAR under 45.5 (-111), ATL–TB under 43.5 (-111), and IND–JAX under 46.5 (-110). The screen uses average wind of at least 10 mph and temperatures from 33 to 90 degrees; displayed history is 635-467-10 with 11% ROI.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: these are source claims, not verified game-time weather effects. Stadium shelter and roof conditions can invalidate an outdoor weather proxy. Historical ROI is not a forecast for these four games.
rows.next_check: Verify venue, roof/open-air exposure and forecast near kickoff; compare the exact current total and price. Re-capture tomorrow before a new decision. No automatic wind adjustment.
rows.quote_status: Source-pick benchmark only; no verified executable sportsbook quote

rows.title: Portland–Utah: investigate the under
rows.observation: Action lists Under 232.5 at -112 as a system selection for October 31. Its displayed history is 534 wins, 434 losses, 9 pushes and 7% ROI. Filters include division games in the regular season, under support at 40% or less, and a total falling by at least one point from open to close.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: closing-line information is unavailable when an earlier ticket is placed. This is a third-party historical screen, not our calibrated win probability. The discovery row and expanded chart also disagree on total units; those units are not used.
rows.next_check: Compare the same sportsbook total at the actual decision time, verify line movement and current injuries/pace, then track an independent forward benchmark. Do not apply a fixed probability boost or copy the source stake.

rows.title: System discovery: win rate alone can mislead
rows.observation: The catalog includes both winning and losing historical screens. Its college-football Sharp Money screen shows 51% wins and -1% ROI; an MLB public-fade moneyline screen shows 59% wins and -3% ROI.
rows.interpretation: Use price-adjusted returns, sample size and forward results; neither a sharp-money label nor a high hit rate proves value. Selecting only the best historical screens risks selection bias.
rows.next_check: Keep source systems separate from agency results; test rules prospectively with timestamped inputs and realistic prices before changing betting behavior.

rows.title: College football: compare external model disagreements
rows.observation: At capture the dashboard displayed South Alabama +6.5 versus projection +2, Air Force +0.5 versus -3.5, and Kansas State +2.5 versus -1.2 for October 31 matchups. These are external model comparison leads, not accepted picks or verified book offers.
rows.interpretation: WATCH: a forecast disagreement identifies something to investigate. It does not establish which model is right. The dashboard supplies no named executable sportsbook for these displayed offers.
rows.next_check: Resolve full team/event identities and current sportsbook contracts, compare our forecast and injuries, and preserve the disagreement for later outcome scoring.

evidence_decisions.note: New paper evaluations use supported fresh evidence. CFBD quality-screen v1 is active for CFB moneylines and laying-points spreads: a joint offensive/defensive disadvantage with four-game samples raises required edge by 2 percentage points and caps stakes at one unit. It can change takes to passes without changing forecast probabilities. Totals and underdog spreads retain existing rules. Experimental, not proven profitable. Injury scenarios can change NBA prop forecasts (maximum 5 percentage points; half-unit stake cap). Falling minutes and matched moneyline crowding can raise required edge. Verified AI caution/reject assessments can tighten or hold a decision; narrative summaries cannot set probabilities. These hypotheses are not proven profitable. Counterpoint keeps its separate inverse experiment; NFL prop holds remain.
limitations: No unattended Action Network collection; snapshots expire after 30 minutes
Spread/total splits need exact source-line identity and remain display-only
Missing evidence retains the original forecast and is explicitly recorded
Existing tickets are never reselected or rewritten

decision_policy.note: Active experimental paper rule: for moneylines and spreads laying points (including pick-em), if the selected team has at least 0.05 lower offensive PPA/play AND at least 0.05 higher defensive PPA allowed than its opponent, require 2 additional percentage points of model edge and cap the stake at one unit. All four overall samples need at least four games and fresh, matched CFBD evidence. Totals, underdog spreads, missing/stale samples and mixed evidence retain existing rules. This is an unvalidated selection screen, not a calibrated probability model. Counterpoint keeps its inverse experiment.

claude_reviews.summary: Top three observations (read-only; no tests run, and saved tests reflect a different source snapshot, so none certify this code). (1) information_intake.py:98 and :100 / shared_research_service.py:50-51: assessments marked can_constrain_paper_decisions flow back via assessments() into candidate() reader fields; they are gated on a 4-hour window and automatic_api_call, but the briefing's per-assessment 'verdict' values are not validated or checked against evidence freshness in shared_research_service.py:50-51 (assessments copied unvetted via p.get('assessments',[])). Hypothesis/missing validation, not a confirmed bug. (2) shared_research_service.py:93: delivery identity=digest([agency,content]) with content including news_reports counts and decisions evaluated against `now` means a new row can be inserted every 30-minute pass whenever any freshness-dependent action (e.g., WATCH vs PASS at :25-26) flips; each insert triggers per-agent record() at :97, so repeated decision-memory entries could inflate counts. Possible duplicate accounting, needs validation. (3) information_intake.py:124 and :84: target tip_utc is compared to game tip with stamp(), and market-context expiry uses created+30min capped at tip_utc; a missing tip_utc (line 84) makes expiry equal created, so the row is immediately expired, which is safe but silently drops ML splits. Also validate() at :27 only rejects sk- style credentials, a narrow secret filter; text field is retained verbatim. Candidate() sets affects_betting=False, so double-adjustment risk with CFB EPA appears contained, but not verifiable from excerpts.

1) cfbd_ppa.py:117-125 vs cfb_efficiency.py:80: the CFBD history filter has no kickoff-time cutoff, only season/week < before_week, and it never confirms that each accepted game's week is strictly earlier than the target game's week at the event level (it relies on season/week equality checks against the schedule). Same-week games are excluded, so leakage looks limited, but mid-week MACtion or bye-week schedule oddities could still slip through; a kickoff < tip_utc guard like the one in cfb_efficiency.py:81 is missing. Hypothesis, needs validation. 2) cfbd_ppa.py:89-93 school() uses a normalized longest-prefix match, which can mis-resolve names such as 'Miami (OH)' vs 'Miami' or 'Texas' vs 'Texas State' when normalization strips punctuation, and line 111 only checks that the name set equals {h,a}. A wrong-team match is possible and is checked only by the team-name set, not by team id; this is an identity risk. 3) cfbd_ppa.py:36-44 and :58: the daily reservation file is created with status 'reserved' before the fetch, and any crash between reserve and final write leaves a permanent 'reserved' receipt for that UTC date. load() at :65-69 reads the latest file with no status check, so attach() silently aborts (status != 'ok') with no retry until the next UTC day. This is safe for quota but means a silent loss of the gate. Also cfb_efficiency.py:206 applies a 0.05 threshold gate that is an unvalidated selection screen. The code does not show it affecting probability, only the threshold. Tests are for a different snapshot and certify nothing.

Top observations (static review; no tests run, and the supplied test receipt is stale). (1) ai_budget.py:65 and 91 plus ai_research_worker.py:263-264: any single 'uncertain' row blocks ALL providers' paid calls indefinitely, and crashed 'reserved' rows are converted to uncertain at worker start with no reconciliation path in the supplied code. This is fail-closed (safe for money) but a likely availability lock-up; hypothesis that a reconcile tool exists elsewhere. (2) ai_budget.py:85 charges 2*inputs*rin while the reserve at line 51 is 2*((bytes+4096)*rin + out*rout), so the cost>reserved check at line 86 could raise on large token counts relative to bytes (tokens can exceed UTF-8 bytes rarely). On ValueError the reservation stays 'reserved' (rollback) and is later forced to 'uncertain' with the full reserve, and the provider call has already occurred. Definite edge risk, low probability. (3) ai_research_worker.py:158 counts Anthropic cache tokens at the uncached rate (conservative, fine), but line 59/60 retry eligibility and ai_budget.py:67 cooldown use started_utc string/time comparisons; retry bypasses cooldown only via recovery flag, and a 429 retry for OpenAI uses job_key 'retry:'+id, allowing one retry per prior id, so chains of retries on new rejected rows are possible within daily count limits (hypothesis). Also note ai_research_worker.py:112-113 hashes the review_key with week, so the weekly dedup works, but line 64-66 research evidence 'probability_adjustment' fields are passed to the reader, which is acceptable given the prompt forbids double boosts. No temporal leakage was found in the supplied excerpts; freshness windows are applied at lines 64, 70, 79 and 94.

bankroll_policy: New paper stakes: at most 40% committed overall, 10% per sport, 2% per game and 1% per ticket. At most 10% committed beyond 24 hours. Sportsbook NBA/NFL game lines may use 7.5% per sport, leaving 2.5% of bankroll for props within the 10% sport limit. Percentages use the lower of initial bankroll and current cash plus open stakes; profits do not automatically increase limits. Existing locked tickets remain intact, and may exceed new limits until settlement. Model and sportsbook accounts stay separate.
